fleet-cluster.1: Share of desired Git repositories that are ready on the selected clusters. A value of 100% means all desired repositories are ready; with no desired repositories the ratio is undefined. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster.2: Current counts of desired and ready Git repositories across the selected clusters. A gap means that some repository deployments are not ready. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster.3: Desired and ready Git repository counts over time for the selected clusters. A persistent gap indicates incomplete deployment. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster.4: Share of desired Kubernetes resources that Fleet reports as ready. With no desired resources the ratio is undefined. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster.5: Current resource counts by Fleet state: desired, ready, not ready, missing, modified, unknown, orphaned, and waiting to be applied. These categories can overlap and should not be added together. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster.6: Resource counts by Fleet state over time. Missing means an expected resource was not found; modified means the live resource differs from the desired version; orphaned means it is no longer managed. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster.7: Share of selected Fleet clusters in the Ready state. An empty selection has no defined readiness ratio. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster.8: Current cluster counts split into Ready, NotReady, and WaitCheckIn. WaitCheckIn means Fleet is waiting for the downstream agent to report. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster.9: Cluster counts by readiness state over time. A sustained NotReady or WaitCheckIn state warrants checking the Fleet agent and cluster connectivity. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.

fleet-cluster-group.1: Share of desired bundle deployments that are ready in the selected cluster groups. A bundle is a package of Kubernetes resources managed by Fleet; no desired bundles means the ratio is undefined. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster-group.2: Current desired and ready bundle counts for the selected cluster groups. A gap indicates that deployments are still pending or unhealthy. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster-group.3: Desired and ready bundle counts over time for the selected cluster groups. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster-group.4: Share of clusters that are ready, calculated as total minus non-ready clusters divided by total. With no clusters the ratio is undefined. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster-group.5: Current total and non-ready cluster counts in the selected groups. The non-ready count is a subset of the total. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster-group.6: Total and non-ready cluster counts over time for the selected groups. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster-group.7: Share of desired resources that are ready in the selected cluster groups. With no desired resources the ratio is undefined. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster-group.8: Current Kubernetes resource counts by Fleet state for the selected groups. Desired and ready are compared with missing, modified, orphaned, unknown, and waiting-to-apply counts; these categories can overlap. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-cluster-group.9: Resource counts by Fleet state over time for the selected groups. Persistent missing, modified, or non-ready resources can explain incomplete bundle deployment. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.

fleet-gitrepo.1: Share of desired target clusters where the selected Git repositories are ready. With no desired clusters the ratio is undefined. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitrepo.2: Current desired and ready target cluster counts for the selected Git repositories. A gap indicates incomplete rollout. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitrepo.3: Desired and ready target cluster counts over time for the selected Git repositories. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitrepo.4: Share of desired Kubernetes resources reported ready for the selected Git repositories. With no desired resources the ratio is undefined. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitrepo.5: Current resource counts by Fleet state for the selected Git repositories. Desired and ready are compared with not-ready, missing, modified, and unknown counts; these categories can overlap. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitrepo.6: Resource counts by Fleet state over time for the selected Git repositories. Modified resources differ from the Git-defined desired state. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.

fleet-bundledeployment.1: Share of bundle deployments in the Ready state in the selected cluster namespaces. Each deployment applies one Fleet bundle to a target cluster; an empty selection has no defined ratio. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-bundledeployment.2: Current bundle deployment counts by state. WaitApplied and Pending indicate unfinished work, ErrApplied indicates an apply error, and OutOfSync or Modified indicate a difference from the desired state. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-bundledeployment.3: Bundle deployment counts by state over time in the selected cluster namespaces. Sustained non-ready states indicate incomplete or unhealthy deployment. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.

fleet-bundle.1: Share of desired bundle targets that are ready for the selected bundles. Bundles are packages of Kubernetes resources deployed by Fleet; with no desired targets the ratio is undefined. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-bundle.2: Current desired, ready, and non-ready bundle target counts, with pending, apply-error, out-of-sync, modified, and waiting-to-apply states. Some counts overlap and should not be summed. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-bundle.3: Bundle target counts by readiness and deployment state over time. Compare ready with desired to see whether deployment has converged. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.

fleet-gitjob.2: Estimated p99 duration in seconds for fetching the latest Git commit, grouped by repository. About 99% of observations complete within this duration. Uses the automatic rate window; no completed operations produce no percentile, and non-positive values are omitted. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitjob.3: Estimated p90 duration in seconds for fetching the latest Git commit, grouped by repository. About 90% of observations complete within this duration. Uses the automatic rate window; no completed operations produce no percentile, and non-positive values are omitted. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitjob.4: Estimated p50 duration in seconds for fetching the latest Git commit, grouped by repository. About 50% of observations complete within this duration. Uses the automatic rate window; no completed operations produce no percentile, and non-positive values are omitted. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitjob.5: Distribution of durations in seconds for fetching the latest Git commit, using observations accumulated over the selected dashboard period. Histogram buckets count operations up to each duration boundary; an idle period can have no observations. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitjob.6: Duration distribution over time for fetching the latest Git commit. Each heatmap slice uses the automatic rate window; color represents the number of observations and the duration axis is in seconds. Empty slices can simply mean no jobs ran. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitjob.8: Estimated p99 duration in seconds for running a GitJob, grouped by repository. About 99% of observations complete within this duration. Uses the automatic rate window; no completed operations produce no percentile, and non-positive values are omitted. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitjob.9: Estimated p90 duration in seconds for running a GitJob, grouped by repository. About 90% of observations complete within this duration. Uses the automatic rate window; no completed operations produce no percentile, and non-positive values are omitted. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitjob.10: Estimated p50 duration in seconds for running a GitJob, grouped by repository. About 50% of observations complete within this duration. Uses the automatic rate window; no completed operations produce no percentile, and non-positive values are omitted. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitjob.11: Distribution of durations in seconds for running a GitJob, using observations accumulated over the selected dashboard period. Histogram buckets count operations up to each duration boundary; an idle period can have no observations. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-gitjob.12: Duration distribution over time for running a GitJob. Each heatmap slice uses the automatic rate window; color represents the number of observations and the duration axis is in seconds. Empty slices can simply mean no jobs ran. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.

fleet-controller-runtime.1: Number of controller workers currently processing reconciliation tasks. Reconciliation compares actual Kubernetes state with the desired state. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.2: Reconciliation errors per second, averaged over five minutes and grouped by instance and pod. Despite the title this is an error rate, not a cumulative count. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.3: Reconciliation attempts per second, averaged over five minutes and grouped by instance and pod. Despite the title this is a processing rate. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.4: Number of items currently waiting in each controller work queue. A persistent increase can mean workers are not keeping up. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.5: Median (p50) time in seconds that an item waited before processing, estimated from the last five minutes. No processed items means no latency estimate. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.6: p90 queue waiting time in seconds over the last five minutes: about 90% of items waited less than this. An idle queue can have no latency observations. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.7: p99 queue waiting time in seconds over the last five minutes: about 99% of items waited less than this. This highlights unusually long waits; idle queues can have no observations. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.8: Items added to each controller queue per second, averaged over two minutes. Compare with processing rates and queue depth to identify growing backlogs. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.9: The current query applies a five-minute rate to the unfinished-work duration gauge. It shows a derived change rate, not the current age or total duration of unfinished tasks; interpret it cautiously because rate assumes a counter. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.10: Median (p50) processing duration in seconds for queue items, estimated over five minutes. This excludes time waiting in the queue; no completed work means no estimate. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.11: p90 processing duration in seconds for queue items over five minutes. About 90% of measured tasks finish within this duration; idle queues can have no observations. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.12: p99 processing duration in seconds for queue items over five minutes. This highlights slow processing; idle queues can have no observations. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.
fleet-controller-runtime.13: Queue retries per second, averaged over five minutes and grouped by instance and queue. Sustained retries can indicate errors or repeatedly unmet dependencies. No data can mean that Fleet metrics are not collected or that no objects match the selected filters.

nginx.20: Total HTTP requests per second across the selected controllers. Uses the latest pair of samples within two minutes, so brief traffic spikes remain visible. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.82: Active NGINX connections, summed across selected controllers after averaging each series over two minutes. Connections include more than currently executing requests. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.21: Fraction of responses that are neither HTTP 4xx nor 5xx, calculated from two-minute request rates. This is undefined when there is no traffic; redirects count as successful here. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.81: Average successful configuration reloads per minute across selected controllers, derived from the latest counter samples within one minute. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.83: Number of selected controller instances whose latest configuration reload failed. An empty result can mean no failures because the query filters out successful instances; it can also mean metrics are missing. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.86: HTTP requests per second grouped by ingress, based on the latest samples within two minutes. Helps identify which route is receiving traffic. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.87: Fraction of non-4xx/non-5xx responses per ingress over two minutes. No requests means the success ratio is undefined; redirects count as successful. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.32: Request and response traffic in bytes per second from the latest samples within two minutes. Responses are drawn below zero only to distinguish direction, not because traffic is negative. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.77: Average resident memory in bytes per selected NGINX process. This is an average across processes, not the total controller memory footprint. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.79: Average CPU usage per NGINX process in CPU cores over two minutes. A value of 1 means one fully used core; this is not a percentage of node capacity. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.75: Per-ingress p50, p90, and p99 request duration in seconds over two minutes, together with request and response byte rates. Percentiles describe the duration below which 50%, 90%, or 99% of requests finish; no traffic means no latency estimate. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
nginx.85: Seconds remaining until the selected TLS certificates expire, grouped by host. Zero is expiry and negative values indicate an expired certificate. Values are averaged if multiple matching certificate series exist. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.

4GFbkOsZk.91: Total request duration in seconds, including NGINX and the upstream response transfer. p50 is the median; p95 and p99 bound approximately 95% and 99% of requests. Estimated over one minute; idle windows have no percentile. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
4GFbkOsZk.94: Time in seconds spent receiving a response from the upstream service, shown as p50, p95, and p99 over one minute. Idle windows have no latency observations. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
4GFbkOsZk.93: Requests per second for each URL path in the selected ingress, averaged over one minute. Helps identify the busiest routes. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
4GFbkOsZk.98: Median upstream response duration in seconds for each URL path, estimated over one minute. Half of measured responses finish within this duration; no requests means no estimate. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
4GFbkOsZk.100: Fraction of HTTP responses with 4xx or 5xx status for each URL path over one minute. With no requests the ratio is undefined; absent error series can also leave a path blank. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
4GFbkOsZk.102: Upstream response time accumulated per second for each URL path, using a one-minute window. Units are seconds of response time per wall-clock second; this measures total work and can exceed 1 when requests overlap. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
4GFbkOsZk.101: HTTP 4xx and 5xx responses per second, grouped by URL path and status code and averaged over one minute. Distinguishes traffic volume of failures from their percentage. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
4GFbkOsZk.99: Average response size in bytes for each URL path, calculated as response bytes divided by response count over one minute. Paths without responses have no average. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.
4GFbkOsZk.96: Mean upstream service latency in seconds for the selected ingress, calculated over one minute from total observed latency divided by observation count. No observations means no latency estimate. Requires NGINX ingress-controller metrics; a cluster using a different ingress controller can correctly show no data here.

cenvey6u87ta8d.6: Number of backup objects currently marked Completed. The query returns zero even when no matching metrics exist, so zero can also mean the backup operator is absent or not scraped. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.5: Number of backup objects whose status is not Completed, including in-progress or failed objects. The query returns zero when no metrics match, including when metrics are unavailable. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.17: Current backup object counts split into recurring and non-recurring definitions. This counts backup objects, not successful backup executions. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.4: Total restore count reported by the backup operator. This is the exported count, not the number of restores within the selected dashboard period. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.7: Cumulative successful recurring backup attempts by name, calculated as attempts minus failures. Counter resets can lower the value; this is not a count restricted to the displayed period. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.14: Cumulative failed recurring backup attempts by name. Counter resets can lower the value; a rising line indicates new failures. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.15: Backup success fraction over the selected SLI window: successful attempt rate divided by total attempt rate. SLI means service-level indicator. Windows with no attempts are omitted rather than treated as 100% successful. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.9: Estimated p99 backup duration in seconds from observations over the selected dashboard period. About 99% of backups complete within this duration; no observations or non-positive estimates are omitted. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.8: Estimated p90 backup duration in seconds from observations over the selected dashboard period. About 90% of backups complete within this duration; no observations or non-positive estimates are omitted. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.10: Median (p50) backup duration in seconds from observations over the selected dashboard period. Half of backups complete within this duration; no observations or non-positive estimates are omitted. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.2: Backup object inventory and status for the selected backup names. Rows come from operator metadata metrics; they describe objects rather than backup file contents or integrity. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.
cenvey6u87ta8d.3: Restore object inventory and status from operator metadata metrics. This lists reported restore objects rather than verifying restored application data. Requires the Rancher backup operator and its metrics; missing operator metrics are not proof that backups are healthy.

rancher-logging-fluentbit.14: Output retries and errors per second, summed across Fluent Bit and averaged over one minute. Persistent retries suggest a slow or unreachable log destination; errors indicate unsuccessful output operations. Requires Fluent Bit logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentbit.44: Input and successfully processed output log records per second, averaged over one minute. Persistent input/output differences can indicate filtering, buffering, or delivery problems. Requires Fluent Bit logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentbit.30: Output retries per second by plugin type over one minute. Despite the title this is a retry rate, not a cumulative retry count. Requires Fluent Bit logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentbit.45: Output errors per second by plugin type over one minute. Sustained errors warrant checking the log destination and Fluent Bit logs. Requires Fluent Bit logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentbit.46: Incoming log records per second by input type, averaged over one minute. Despite the title this is a rate, not a lifetime total. Requires Fluent Bit logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentbit.47: Records dropped by filters per second by type, averaged over one minute. Drops can be intentional filtering; compare with configured rules before treating them as data loss. Requires Fluent Bit logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.

rancher-logging-fluentd.14: Output retries and errors per second over one minute. Occasional retries can be transient; sustained retries suggest a slow or unreachable destination. Errors can indicate unrecoverable processing problems; see https://docs.fluentd.org/buffer#handling-unrecoverable-errors. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.44: Incoming records per second compared with output write operations per second over one minute. A write can contain multiple records, so these two series are not directly comparable record counts. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.20: Lowest reported percentage of free output-buffer capacity across Fluentd outputs. Approaching zero means little capacity remains and log ingestion can block or records can be dropped, depending on configuration. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.21: Rate of accumulated flush time (milliseconds per second) alongside slow flush operations per second, both over one minute. These series use different units; this is not an average per-flush latency. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.13: Current combined stage and queue buffer size in bytes, grouped by output type. Growing buffers can indicate output is not keeping up with incoming logs. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.15: Current number of chunks waiting in output buffer queues, summed across Fluentd. A chunk contains a batch of records; this is not a record count. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.39: Total incoming log records per second, averaged over one minute. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.47: Incoming log records per second by hostname, averaged over one minute. Shows which source hosts generate the most logs. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.60: Incoming log records per second by Kubernetes namespace, averaged over one minute. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.48: Incoming log records per second by scraped Fluentd instance, averaged over one minute. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.49: Incoming log records per second by Fluentd routing tag, averaged over one minute. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.22: Current number of chunks in stage buffers, grouped by pod and output type. Staged chunks are still being accumulated before they enter the flush queue. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.23: Current size of staged buffer chunks in bytes, grouped by pod and output type. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.50: Maximum number of queued output chunks observed within the last minute, per exported series. Helps expose short queue spikes. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.25: Maximum combined buffer size in bytes observed within the last minute, per exported series. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.24: Current number of chunks waiting to be flushed, grouped by pod and output type. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.51: Current queued buffer size in bytes, grouped by pod and output type. Persistent growth can indicate a slow or failing destination. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.26: Sum of reported free-buffer percentages for each pod and output type. If several outputs share the same labels, this sum can exceed 100%; it is not a capacity-weighted free-space percentage. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.30: Output retries per second by output type, averaged over one minute. Despite the title this is a rate rather than the current retry count. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.33: Records emitted to output plugins per second by type, averaged over one minute. Emission does not by itself prove successful delivery to the destination. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.32: Emit operations per second by output type, averaged over one minute. One operation may contain multiple log records. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.35: Output rollback operations per second by type, averaged over one minute. Rollbacks return unsuccessful work for later handling and can accompany delivery failures. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.34: Output write operations per second by type, averaged over one minute. Writes are batches or chunks, not necessarily individual log records. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.37: Slow flush operations per second by output type, averaged over one minute. Persistent slow flushes can indicate a destination throughput bottleneck. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.38: The current query applies a one-minute rate to the retry-wait metric and sums it by output type. This is a derived change per second, not the current retry delay; interpret cautiously if the exporter reports retry wait as a gauge. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.36: Accumulated output flush time in milliseconds per second, averaged over one minute and grouped by output type. This measures total flush time accumulation, not the duration of an individual flush. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.31: Output errors per second by output type, averaged over one minute. Rising errors warrant inspecting Fluentd and the destination. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.29: Seconds between the newest and oldest time keys currently represented in a buffer. A wide span can indicate buffered logs cover a long period; this is not the age of the oldest log relative to now. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.27: Unix timestamp in seconds of the newest buffered time key, summed by pod and output type. A time key identifies a log time partition. Multiple series with the same labels make the summed timestamp hard to interpret. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.
rancher-logging-fluentd.28: Unix timestamp in seconds of the oldest buffered time key, summed by pod and output type. Multiple series with the same labels make the summed timestamp hard to interpret; this is not directly a backlog age. Requires Fluentd logging metrics; no data can mean this optional logging component is not installed or scraped.

tfrfU0a7k.22: The 20 slowest reconciliation handlers by average execution duration in seconds over five minutes. A handler is controller code that reacts to object changes; no executions means no average. Requires Rancher internal performance metrics to be collected; missing series can mean instrumentation is unavailable.
